stem: A random sample of 500 residents of a coastal town was asked whether they support building a seawall. Based on the sample, 64% of the town's residents are estimated to support the seawall, with a margin of error of 4.3 percentage points. Which of the following is NOT a plausible value for the percent of all the town's residents who support the seawall?
solution: The plausible values run from \(64 - 4.3 = 59.7\) percent to \(64 + 4.3 = 68.3\) percent.
Only 69% is outside this interval, so it is not a plausible value.

explanation.A: Incorrect. 67% is between 59.7% and 68.3%, so it is a plausible value.
explanation.B: Correct. 69% is greater than \(64 + 4.3 = 68.3\) percent, so it is not a plausible value.
explanation.C: Incorrect. 62% is between 59.7% and 68.3%, so it is a plausible value.
explanation.D: Incorrect. 60% is greater than 59.7%, so it is inside the interval of plausible values.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
lo, hi = Rational(64) - Rational('4.3'), Rational(64) + Rational('4.3')
pl = {k: lo <= Rational(choices[k].rstrip('%')) <= hi for k in choices}
assert [k for k in pl if not pl[k]] == [answer]
